title: Interop smoke test against a real ACP client over stdio
description:
The verification that cannot be faked by our own test suite: a client we did not write completes a session against python-acp over stdio.

Options are the SDK's own example clients under examples/, or a real editor integration (Zed, Neovim). Prefer something runnable in CI; if nothing is, make it a documented manual procedure with recorded output rather than skipping it.

This is the payoff for decision D2 -- it is the check that 'strict full ACP v1' means something outside this repository.
acceptance_criteria: A third-party ACP client completes initialize, session creation, a prompt turn with streamed updates, and clean shutdown against python-acp over stdio; the procedure is automated in CI or documented as a manual runbook with recorded output; failures are diagnosable from the captured transcript.
notes: pyacp-tzd.2 delivered the stdio binding and a subprocess-level test (tests/test_transport_stdio.py) that drives 'python -m python_acp.cli --transport stdio' with the SDK's own ClientSideConnection via acp.stdio.spawn_agent_process. That covers startup, JSON-RPC framing over a pipe, initialize, and clean exit - but the client is the SDK's, not a third party's, and no session is created because session/new is still -32601 until pyacp-3rw.2. This bead remains the real-client, full-session check.

title: Build the method-by-method ACP conformance suite
description:
Test every method in Phase 0.2's compliance matrix against its disposition: implemented methods behave per spec, declined methods return the correct error. The matrix is the checklist; a method absent from the suite is a gap in the matrix or the suite.

Structure it so adding an Agent method without adding conformance coverage is visibly incomplete. This suite is what makes the Phase 7 removal safe, so it must be trustworthy before that lands.
acceptance_criteria: Every Agent method in the matrix has conformance coverage matching its disposition; declined methods are asserted to return the correct error, not merely to fail; the suite runs under make test on all four matrix Python versions; a new method with no coverage is detectable.
notes: pyacp-4ns.2: cases derive mechanically from docs/acp-compliance-matrix.md, including the declines. See its 'What Phase 8 tests' section - notably the both-directions test for the three unstable-gated methods, and pinning -32601 for session/delete, logout, providers/*, nes/*, and document/* so a future SDK bump that starts routing them is noticed.

title: Call session/request_permission from the turn executor
description:
CORRECTION FROM THE ORIGINAL PLAN: request_permission is an acp.interfaces.Client method. The agent CALLS it; it does not implement it. The original plan's 'Implement session/request_permission' was backwards.

Before a consequential tool call, ask the client for permission with the tool call and the available PermissionOptions, and honor the answer. Handle the cancellation outcome -- the client can cancel the turn while the permission prompt is open, which must land as stopReason cancelled (Phase 3.5), not as a denied permission.

Evaluate acp.contrib.permissions, which ships a permission broker.
acceptance_criteria: The executor requests permission before consequential tool calls and honors allow, deny, and always-variants; cancellation while a prompt is open produces stopReason cancelled; behavior when the client does not support permissions is defined and tested; which tool calls are consequential is documented; whether acp.contrib.permissions is used is recorded with a reason.

title: Get stopReason semantics right, especially cancelled
description:
prompt must return the correct stopReason for every exit path: normal completion, cancellation, refusal, and any limit condition the executor can hit.

'cancelled' is called out in the plan's verification because it is the one most easily got wrong -- a cancelled turn must return the response with stopReason cancelled, not raise, not hang, and not return end_turn. It also has to interleave correctly with in-flight session/update notifications and with an MCP call still running in the backend.

Pairs with Phase 1.5's $/cancel_request registry; these are two different cancellation mechanisms and both must be verified.
acceptance_criteria: Each exit path returns its correct stopReason; cancelling mid-turn returns stopReason cancelled promptly rather than raising or hanging; no session/update notifications are emitted after the turn response; an in-flight MCP call is cancelled or abandoned cleanly; tests cover cancel-before-start, cancel-mid-tool-call, and cancel-after-completion.

title: Emit the full session/update variant set
description:
Emit every SessionNotification variant the SDK defines: UserMessageChunk, AgentMessageChunk, AgentThoughtChunk, ToolCallStart, ToolCallProgress, AgentPlanUpdate, AgentPlanContentUpdate, AgentPlanRemovedUpdate, AvailableCommandsUpdate, CurrentModeUpdate, ConfigOptionUpdate, SessionInfoUpdate, UsageUpdate.

Use acp.helpers for construction and evaluate acp.contrib.tool_calls, which ships a tool-call tracker -- tool call state transitions are the fiddliest part of this and are easy to get subtly wrong.

Some variants only have meaning once their source feature exists (CurrentModeUpdate needs Phase 5.2, ConfigOptionUpdate needs Phase 5.3, UsageUpdate may have no source at all with no LLM). Record which are emitted, which are deferred, and which are declined.
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable variant is emitted with correct ordering and payloads; tool call lifecycle transitions are correct including the failure path; variants with no source are explicitly recorded as deferred or declined rather than silently missing; whether acp.contrib.tool_calls is used is recorded with a reason; golden transcript coverage in Phase 8.2 has something to assert against.

title: Ship the deterministic MCP tool-router turn executor
description:
The default executor: interpret prompt content blocks as explicit MCP tool invocations, run them against the session's MCP backends, stream real tool_call and tool_call_update notifications, and return end_turn. No reasoning, no model.

Define and document the input convention -- how a content block names a tool and carries arguments -- since this is the contract every client of this executor codes against, and it is invented here rather than given by the spec.

Decide the behavior for prompts that do not parse as a tool invocation: error, or a message chunk explaining the convention.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt content mapped to MCP tool calls by a documented convention; tool_call and tool_call_update notifications carry real status transitions and results; multiple tool calls in one turn work; unparseable prompts produce a defined, tested outcome; end_turn returned on success; the convention is documented in the README and the module doc.
notes:
pyacp-db3 built the backend this bead routes through. Seams:
- PythonAcpAgent.backends is an McpBackendRegistry; registry.backends(session_id) returns
  {name: MCPStdioClient} for that session, registry.get(session_id, name) raises
  UnknownBackendError (a ValueError -> -32602) for a name the session did not open.
- Servers are opened AND handshaked during session/new, so an executor can assume every
  client it gets is live. Opening is all-or-nothing; a session whose servers failed does
  not exist.
- Names are unique per session (enforced in McpBackendRegistry.open) precisely so this
  bead can route a tool call by server name.
- TurnContext does NOT carry backends -- module-boundaries has turn_mcp_router.py reach
  mcp_registry.py directly, so construct the executor with the registry rather than
  widening the context.
- Each session gets its OWN subprocess even when two sessions name the same server; do not
  add sharing without preserving close-independence.

title: Define the TurnExecutor interface
description:
Decision D3's seam. Define the interface a prompt turn runs behind: it receives the session and its content blocks, may call client methods (Phase 4), emits session/update notifications, and returns a stopReason.

This is what makes 'no LLM in the loop' a design choice rather than a dead end, and it satisfies the original Phase 6.3 'backend abstraction for non-MCP executors' in the same stroke.

Design it so an LLM-backed executor is droppable in later without reopening the interface -- specifically, do not assume the turn is synchronous, single-step, or free of client round-trips.
acceptance_criteria: A documented TurnExecutor interface with streaming update emission, client-method access, cancellation, and stopReason return; the deterministic executor and at least one test double both implement it; the interface does not assume a single-step or non-interactive turn; sibling .md written; the seam is reflected in ARCHITECTURE.md.
notes:
pyacp-3rw.2 seeded src/python_acp/turns.py because this bead depends on it and
session/prompt had to be wired to something; putting a provisional seam in agent.py would
have violated module-boundaries (agent.py is method-shaped translation only). Recorded as
decision B6b.

What is there: TurnExecutor Protocol with one `async execute(context, prompt) -> StopReason`;
TurnContext(session, client) exposing session_id and `emit(update)` (which supplies the
session id itself so an executor cannot address another session); IdleTurnExecutor, the
default that completes a turn having done nothing and logs a warning.

Because the call is async and single-method, nothing assumes the turn is synchronous,
single-step, or free of client round-trips -- this bead's stated constraint.

What this bead must STILL add (also listed in src/python_acp/turns.md):
- stopReason beyond end_turn/cancelled: max_tokens, max_turn_requests, refusal (hnk.5)
- capability-gated client-method access; context.client is the raw facade today
- a cancellation token, so an executor can run async cleanup without racing the cancel
- content-block typing; `prompt` is list[Any] and the promptCapabilities literals stay
  false in AGENT_CAPABILITY_MANIFEST until hnk.3 enforces them
- a TurnResult carrying usage; PromptResponse.usage exists and nothing fills it

agent.py already owns the cancelled path: the turn runs as its own task and
asyncio.wait({turn}) + turn.cancelled() distinguishes "session/cancel reached it" from
"this request was cancelled". Do not change that to `await turn` -- it makes the two
indistinguishable.

title: Implement the baseline session lifecycle: new_session, prompt, cancel, session_update
description:
The minimum viable ACP session: create one, prompt it, stream updates back, cancel it. This is the path a real client exercises first and the one Phase 8's interop smoke test depends on.

prompt's body is Phase 3's turn executor -- here, wire the plumbing and the session/update emission channel, not the turn semantics.

session/cancel must cooperatively stop the running turn; the stopReason 'cancelled' contract is Phase 3.5.
acceptance_criteria: new_session creates a registry entry and returns a valid NewSessionResponse; prompt dispatches to the turn executor and streams session/update notifications to the client; cancel stops an in-flight turn; a client can run the full create-prompt-cancel cycle over stdio; tests cover each step and the cancel-with-no-turn-running case.
notes:
pyacp-3rw.1 built the registry this bead wires up. Seams already in place:
- SessionRegistry.create(cwd, additional_directories=, modes=, config_options=, title=)
  returns a Session; agent.py should hold ONE registry per process (not per connection --
  it is shared across WebSocket connections so a disconnect cannot delete a session another
  connection may resume).
- Session.attach_turn(task) / detach_turn() / cancel_turn() is where session/cancel reaches.
  attach_turn raises TurnAlreadyRunningError (-> -32603) on a second concurrent prompt;
  cancel_turn() returns False for an idle session, which is NOT an error (session/cancel is
  a notification and a client cancelling a finished turn is behaving correctly).
- UnknownSessionError subclasses ValueError, so errors.to_request_error already maps a
  stale sessionId to -32602 with the id in data.reason. No special case needed.
- Path validation is deliberately absent from the registry; pyacp-3rw.4 owns it at the edge.
close_reason: new_session/prompt/cancel live against SessionRegistry; turns.py seeded with the TurnExecutor seam (decision B6b, hnk.1 completes it); IdleTurnExecutor as the honest default. Turn runs as a task so session/cancel reaches it; asyncio.wait+turn.cancelled() distinguishes turn-cancelled from request-cancelled. One registry per process, required on the agent. session/new rejects unadvertised MCP transports. Full create-prompt-cancel cycle verified over a spawned stdio process and over WebSocket. 234 tests pass.

title: Build the session registry with cwd, additionalDirectories, mode, config, and timestamps
description:
There is no session concept in the runtime at all -- session/* currently returns -32601. Introduce a registry holding, per session: id, cwd, additionalDirectories, current mode, config option state, creation and last-activity timestamps, and the handle to its MCP backend(s).

Evaluate acp.contrib.session_state before writing one; the SDK ships a session accumulator that may cover most of this.

Session state is what makes fork_session and resume_session meaningful in Phase 2.4, so decide the copy-versus-share semantics for backends and history here rather than later.
acceptance_criteria: A session registry exists with the full metadata set; sessions are addressable by id; lifetime is defined (creation, expiry or explicit close, cleanup of backends on close); copy-versus-share semantics for fork and resume are documented; whether acp.contrib.session_state is used or replaced is recorded with a reason; the new module ships its sibling .md.
close_reason: sessions.py + sessions.md + 35 tests. acp.contrib.session_state evaluated and replaced (client-side accumulator, single-session, no metadata, experimental) with the reason recorded in the module doc; noted as the right tool for load_session history on pyacp-3rw.3. Fork=deep copy/own backends/starts idle, resume=shares, documented and tested. Lifetime: no idle expiry, explicit close, on_close hook as the mcp_registry seam (module-boundaries B6a). 214 tests pass.

title: Add a request registry and cooperative cancellation for $/cancel_request
description:
There is no cancellation anywhere in the runtime today. Add a per-connection registry of in-flight requests and cooperative cancellation driven by $/cancel_request, so a client can abandon work rather than wait out a timeout.

Distinct from session/cancel (Phase 3.5), which cancels a prompt turn and must produce stopReason 'cancelled'. This one cancels an individual JSON-RPC request. Both must work; they are different mechanisms and the plan's verification calls for both to be tested.

Interacts with pyacp-ua1: when a cancelled request has an MCP call in flight, the backend should be told via notifications/cancelled rather than left computing a reply nobody reads.
acceptance_criteria: In-flight requests are tracked per connection and cancellable by id; $/cancel_request cancels cooperatively without killing the connection or sibling requests; a cancelled request produces the correct ACP error; cancellation propagates to an in-flight MCP call; tests cover cancelling mid-flight, cancelling an unknown id, and cancelling an already-completed request.
notes:
pyacp-4ns.3 finding: grep of SDK 0.12.1 meta.py, connection.py, and router.py turns up no route or constant for $/cancel_request anywhere. AGENT_METHODS carries session/cancel only. So either $/cancel_request is ours to add (likely via ext_method plus our own request registry) or the requirement is stale. Confirm against acp.interfaces under pyacp-4ns.2 before starting.
pyacp-4ns.2 re-confirmed against the installed 0.12.1: no $/cancel_request route exists in acp/meta.py, acp/router.py, or acp/agent/router.py. ACP cancellation is the session/cancel notification (CancelNotification -> Agent.cancel), which pyacp-3rw.2 and pyacp-hnk.5 already cover. Either this bead means the JSON-RPC-level cancel and must build it on ext_method, or it is a misreading of the spec and should be closed against session/cancel. Decide before implementing.

pyacp-tzd.6 finding, for the "$/cancel_request has no home" question: acp.schema.Error accepts -32800 in its code literal union, alongside the six JSON-RPC standard codes and ACP's -32000/-32002. acp.RequestError supplies NO constructor for it and the schema carries no description; it appears nowhere else in the SDK. -32800 is LSP's RequestCancelled, which ACP's error shape otherwise mirrors. Could not confirm against upstream ACP docs (schema/rust sources 404 at the URLs tried). errors.py now exposes REQUEST_CANCELLED = -32800 and request_cancelled(reason=None) on that reading, with the uncertainty documented in errors.md; confirm before putting it on the wire. Also settled by tzd.6: asyncio.CancelledError is never mapped to a RequestError -- to_request_error re-raises it, because returning a value from a cancelled coroutine tells asyncio the cancellation did not take. Whatever reports a cancellation must do so after letting the exception propagate.

title: Implement initialize negotiation with accurate capabilities and auth methods
description:
Today's initialize returns a hand-built block of literals: loadSession false, promptCapabilities all false, mcpCapabilities http/sse false, auth.logout null, sessionCapabilities delete/additionalDirectories null, authMethods empty. The acp-protocol skill is explicit that this block is a PROMISE, not a reflection of runtime state.

Rebuild it from Phase 0.2's compliance matrix using the SDK's InitializeResponse model, and capture the incoming clientCapabilities -- Phase 4 gates every client call on them, so they must be stored per-connection and reachable from the turn executor.

_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1 is the ACP version and is unrelated to the MCP protocolVersion string in MCPStdioClient.initialize. Two protocols, two version fields; do not merge them.
acceptance_criteria: The advertised capability block matches implemented behavior with no aspirational literals; every advertised capability has a test proving the feature exists; clientCapabilities from the request are stored per-connection and readable by the turn executor; version negotiation follows the ACP spec; a literal cannot be flipped without a corresponding feature test.
notes: pyacp-4ns.2: build AgentCapabilities from the 'Consequences for the initialize capability block' table in docs/acp-compliance-matrix.md and nothing else. Every literal there is owned by a row and flips in the same commit as that row. authMethods is [] deliberately - that is what makes Agent.authenticate an explicit typed refusal rather than a -32601.
close_reason: Capability block compiled from AGENT_CAPABILITY_MANIFEST in src/python_acp/capabilities.py; evidence guard, SDK-coverage walk, and version negotiation tested. Matrix amended with sessionCapabilities.fork/.resume/.close.

title: Bind the stdio transport and add a CLI entry point for it
description:
Decision D2: stdio is the primary ACP transport. This is the issue that makes python-acp connectable by a real ACP client -- Zed, Neovim, or the SDK's own example client -- for the first time.

Bind acp.stdio to the Phase 1.1 agent. Add a CLI mode that speaks ACP on stdin/stdout, which means the process can no longer print to stdout: cli.py currently does 'print(f"python-acp listening on ws://...")' and logging.basicConfig writes to stderr by default but must be verified. Anything on stdout that is not a JSON-RPC message corrupts the stream.

--mcp-command stays as the backend spec; only the client-facing transport is new.
acceptance_criteria: python-acp runs as an ACP agent over stdio; a real ACP client completes initialize and a session over the subprocess; NOTHING besides JSON-RPC messages is ever written to stdout in stdio mode; --debug logging goes to stderr; cli.md updated; the WebSocket mode still works unchanged.
notes: pyacp-4ns.3 decision B6: cli.py:38 currently does print(f"python-acp listening on ws://..."). In stdio transport mode that one line corrupts the JSON-RPC stream. Removing it is in scope for this issue, not a drive-by: cli.py must emit all diagnostics through logging to stderr in every mode. This issue also owns the new transport_stdio.py module plus its sibling transport_stdio.md, and the --transport stdio|ws selector in cli.py (update cli.md).
close_reason: transport_stdio.py + transport_stdio.md + --transport {ws,stdio} in cli.py, with cli.md rewritten. run_stdio passes use_unstable_protocol=True. print() banner removed; configure_logging names sys.stderr; run_stdio additionally swaps sys.stdout to stderr after binding (POSIX only - the SDK's Windows stdio transport resolves sys.stdout at write time). 10 new tests spawn the real subprocess and drive it with the SDK's ClientSideConnection; one asserts every stdout line parses as JSON-RPC. ws mode unchanged and still the default. PARTIAL vs acceptance: 'completes initialize AND a session' - the session half is not deliverable here, session/new is -32601 until pyacp-3rw.2, and third-party-client interop remains pyacp-6ni.4 (noted there).

title: Implement the acp.Agent skeleton on acp.agent.connection
description:
The keystone change. Implement acp.interfaces.Agent as a class wired to acp.agent.connection, with every method present -- returning a method-not-found style error where Phase 0.2's matrix says 'decline' -- so later phases fill in bodies rather than restructure.

This is where dispatch stops being ours. acp.agent.router handles JSON-RPC correlation and dispatch; the hand-rolled _dispatch/_dispatch_jsonrpc path in ws_bridge.py is superseded.

Keep the MCP passthrough working the whole time -- see Phase 7 for how the legacy surface is carried.
acceptance_criteria: An acp.Agent implementation exists with all 16 protocol methods; the SDK's connection layer serves them; declined methods return the correct ACP error rather than raising; existing MCP passthrough behavior still reachable; the new module ships its sibling .md; make lint && make test green.
notes:
pyacp-4ns.3 decision B5: do not build on AgentSideConnection directly. SDK 0.12.1's acp/__init__.py:108 marks direct AgentSideConnection use deprecated and redirects to acp.run_agent, which constructs the connection, runs listen(), and shields close(). transport_stdio.py and transport_ws.py call acp.run_agent; PythonAcpAgent receives its Client handle via on_connect(conn) (AgentSideConnection.__init__ calls on_connect(self)). acp.interfaces.Agent at 0.12.1 has 15 members, not 16: initialize, new_session, load_session, list_sessions, set_session_mode, set_config_option, authenticate, prompt, fork_session, resume_session, close_session, cancel, ext_method, ext_notification, on_connect. Per-method disposition is pyacp-4ns.2's call, not this one's.

pyacp-4ns.2 (docs/acp-compliance-matrix.md): pass use_unstable_protocol=True to acp.run_agent (it takes the kwarg at acp/core.py:44 and forwards it to build_agent_router). session/close, session/fork, and session/resume are registered unstable=True; with the flag off, acp/router.py:65-71 emits a UserWarning and raises method_not_found WITHOUT calling our method, so pyacp-3rw.3 would be dead code. The flag is protocol-visible, so it belongs here with the connection rather than being discovered in Phase 2.
close_reason: src/python_acp/agent.py + agent.md + tests/test_agent.py (24 tests, driven through build_agent_router). All 15 acp.interfaces.Agent members present (the bead said 16; the Protocol has 15). initialize/authenticate/cancel/ext_notification/on_connect live; the rest raise method_not_found, identical to the router's absent-attribute behaviour, so later phases change a body only. Not bound to a transport - that is tzd.2/tzd.3, which must pass use_unstable_protocol=True. MCP passthrough untouched and still reachable via ws_bridge.py. make lint clean; 70 passed, 2 pre-existing sandbox bind() failures (pyacp-22w).

title: Derive the ACP v1 compliance matrix from acp.interfaces
description:
Read the surface off the SDK instead of hand-freezing it from the schema. acp.interfaces.Agent is the Protocol we implement (initialize, new_session, load_session, list_sessions, fork_session, resume_session, close_session, set_session_mode, set_config_option, authenticate, prompt, cancel, ext_method, ext_notification, on_connect). acp.interfaces.Client is what the client implements and we consume.

Produce a matrix recording, per Agent method: implement / stub / decline, and why. Same for each Client method we intend to call, with the clientCapabilities gate that governs it. This matrix is the contract the Phase 8 conformance suite tests against and the source of truth for the initialize capability block in Phase 1.4.

Flag fork_session explicitly -- it is in the SDK's Agent protocol and was missing from the original plan.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in matrix covering every acp.interfaces.Agent and Client method with an explicit disposition and rationale; the initialize capability block in Phase 1.4 is derivable from it with no aspirational entries; it is linked from docs/full-apc-plan.md.
close_reason: docs/acp-compliance-matrix.md: disposition + rationale for all 15 acp.interfaces.Agent members and all 14 Client members, derived from the installed agent-client-protocol==0.12.1 and verified against the built router. Includes the initialize capability block each literal is owned by, the three SDK mechanics that constrain dispositions (decline-by-omission, unstable gating on close/fork/resume, 16 of 28 AGENT_METHODS unrouted), and the Phase 8 test derivation. Linked from full-apc-plan.md, module-boundaries.md, README, ARCHITECTURE.

title: Define module boundaries for the SDK-based runtime
description:
Decide the module layout before code moves, so the co-located docs and ARCHITECTURE.md diagrams get written once against the real shape rather than chased.

Boundaries to place: agent runtime (the acp.Agent implementation), session registry, turn executor, MCP backend adapter, and the transport bindings. Today everything client-facing is one 272-line ws_bridge.py holding both dispatch surfaces; that does not survive contact with Phase 2.

Decide what happens to ws_bridge.py specifically -- renamed, split, or reduced to a transport binding -- since the repo-docs-sync skill ties module basenames to doc basenames and a rename drags ws_bridge.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and the README with it.
acceptance_criteria: A written module layout naming each new module and its responsibility; the fate of ws_bridge.py decided and recorded; the plan for which sibling .md files are created, renamed, or retired is explicit; ARCHITECTURE.md's subsystem diagram updated to the target shape.
notes: Design landed in docs/module-boundaries.md (290 lines): 11-module flat layout, ws_bridge.py split four ways with the rename mechanics, doc create/rename/retire table, target Mermaid diagram mirrored into ARCHITECTURE.md. SDK facts were read from github.com/agentclientprotocol/python-sdk at tag 0.12.1 (byte-identical to main@e668ed9 for interfaces.py, core.py, agent/connection.py, _transport.py, ws/server.py) because the SDK is not installed and PyPI is unreachable here. Everything unconfirmed is listed under 'Pending verification' and deferred to pyacp-4ns.1 (pin) and pyacp-4ns.2 (compliance matrix). Notes appended to pyacp-tzd.1, tzd.2, tzd.3, tzd.5, 4ns.4 where this design corrects their premises. No .py files touched.
close_reason: Implemented, reviewed, and merged to local main. caq=0ce58a6 (venv stamp + pinned .venv + venv_bootstrap.py), 4ns.3=fc214a6 (docs/module-boundaries.md + ARCHITECTURE target diagram), a92=59f97d2 (nextCursor walk with repeated-cursor and page-ceiling bounds). Merged main: ruff clean, 23 passed / 2 failed, both failures the pre-existing pyacp-22w socket.bind PermissionError. Not pushed.

title: Add agent-client-protocol to pyproject and validate it across the CI matrix
description:
Take the SDK dependency (decision D1). PyPI 'agent-client-protocol' 0.12.1, GitHub agentclientprotocol/python-sdk, actively maintained, requires-python >=3.10,<3.15 -- which covers our whole 3.11-3.14 range but also caps us below 3.15, so the ci.yml matrix and the pyproject classifiers now have an upper bound they did not have before. Note that its runtime dependency is pydantic>=2.7; this project is currently zero-dependency apart from websockets.

Do NOT confuse it with PyPI 'acp-sdk', which is IBM's Agent Communication Protocol -- an unrelated protocol with the same abbreviation.

The SDK also ships an 'http' extra pulling websockets>=12.0 and httpx; determine whether the ws transport we want in Phase 1.3 lives behind that extra.

Only 3.11 and 3.14 are installed on this machine; 3.12/3.13 are absent and will NOT be installed. Do not block this bead on multi-version local validation. title: Phase 2: ACP session lifecycle and state
description:
Give the runtime real sessions: a durable registry holding cwd, additionalDirectories, mode and config state, and timestamps, plus the full lifecycle method set.

Replaces the current shape, where one MCP server is bound at process start via --mcp-command and shared by every connected client, with per-session MCP server registries driven by new_session's mcpServers.

Note fork_session is in the SDK's Agent protocol and was missing from the original plan.

title: Phase 3: Prompt turn execution and streaming semantics
description:
Make session/prompt actually do something. Decision D3: a pluggable TurnExecutor interface with a deterministic MCP tool-router as the shipped default -- no LLM, consistent with the project's stated architecture, and an LLM-backed executor can be added later without reopening the design.

The original plan never specified what a prompt turn does with no LLM in the loop, which blocked this phase entirely. That gap is now closed by D3.

Covers the full session/update variant set and correct stopReason semantics.

title: Phase 1: ACP agent runtime foundation
description:
Stand up the agent runtime on the SDK: implement the acp.Agent skeleton, bind both transports, negotiate initialize honestly, and get cancellation and error mapping right.

Decision D2: stdio is the primary transport (that is how Zed, Neovim, and every other ACP client connects); WebSocket is retained as a second binding for the existing local-automation use case. The core runtime is transport-agnostic.

This is the blocking phase. Phase 2 and everything downstream depend on it.

title: Phase 0: ACP v1 contract and SDK substrate adoption
description:
Adopt the agent-client-protocol Python SDK as the substrate for strict ACP v1, and pin down the surface we implement before any of it gets written.

Decision D1 in docs/full-apc-plan.md: build on PyPI 'agent-client-protocol' (GitHub agentclientprotocol/python-sdk), not a hand-rolled dispatcher. The SDK ships generated Pydantic schema models, JSON-RPC plumbing, and both transports we need, so the work becomes implementing acp.interfaces.Agent against our MCP backend rather than building a JSON-RPC server.

Blocks every other ACP v1 epic.

title: MCPStdioClient never drains subprocess stderr
description: start() creates the subprocess with stderr=PIPE but nothing ever reads it. A chatty MCP server fills the pipe buffer and deadlocks the bridge. Either drain stderr into the logger or stop piping it.
close_reason: Background stderr drain task added in 77b3a68 with a reproducing regression test

title: MCPStdioClient drops server-initiated requests and notifications
description: _read_response discards any message whose id does not match the pending request id. MCP servers can call back into the client (sampling/createMessage, roots/list, elicitation/create) and send notifications; those are silently dropped. Blocks real bidirectional MCP client support.
close_reason: Background read loop routes responses, server requests, and notifications in 7114a96

title: Support runtime-configured MCP servers via session/new mcpServers
description: python-acp currently binds ONE MCP server at startup via --mcp-command in cli.py, shared by all WebSocket clients. ACP v1 has the client pass mcpServers in session/new, making the agent an MCP client to N per-session servers. Needs a connection registry keyed by session, replacing the single MCPStdioClient held by ACPWebSocketBridge.
notes:
pyacp-4ns.2: mcpCapabilities.http/sse/acp all stay false, so this bead must ACCEPT McpServerStdio entries on session/new and REJECT HttpMcpServer, SseMcpServer, and AcpMcpServer. McpServerStdio needs no capability flag; the three booleans gate transports we do not drive. Advertising one without implementing its transport is exactly the failure the matrix exists to prevent.
pyacp-3rw.2 findings:
1. session/new ALREADY REJECTS well-formed HttpMcpServer/SseMcpServer/AcpMcpServer entries
   with -32602 (agent._reject_unsupported_mcp_servers), because mcpCapabilities.http/.sse/
   .acp are false in AGENT_CAPABILITY_MANIFEST and accepting one would make the
   advertisement a lie. This bead owns SPAWNING the McpServerStdio entries, which are
   currently accepted and then ignored.
2. HAZARD inherited from the SDK: NewSessionRequest.mcp_servers carries a
   `skip_invalid_items` wrap validator, so any entry that fails validation is SILENTLY
   DROPPED before the agent sees it. Verified: {'name':'t','command':'/bin/true','args':[]}
   disappears entirely because `env` is a REQUIRED field on McpServerStdio (as are
   `headers` on Http/SseMcpServer). A client with a typo gets a session whose server is
   simply absent, with no error. We cannot refuse what never arrives; if that matters,
   this bead has to re-validate the raw params via _meta or accept the behaviour. Pinned by
   tests/test_agent.py::test_a_malformed_mcp_server_is_dropped_before_we_see_it.
3. McpServerStdio required fields: name, command, args, env (all four).
close_reason: mcp_registry.py + .md + 16 tests: per-session McpBackendRegistry, spawn+handshake at session/new, all-or-nothing open, own subprocess per session, env overlaid on os.environ. mcp_stdio gained an env field. agent.new_session opens backends and closes the session if any fail. --mcp-command optional (decision B6c); legacy_ws is its only consumer, follow-up filed under Phase 7. cli wires SessionRegistry(on_close=backends.close). 255 tests pass; verified end-to-end over stdio with no --mcp-command.

title: Final architecture and module documentation refresh
description:
The consistency pass, run once the module boundaries have stopped moving. Documentation is no longer a phase of its own -- the original Phase 7 workstream is complete and repo-docs-sync enforces co-located docs per change -- so this issue only closes the drift that accumulates across eight phases of refactoring.

Check specifically: ARCHITECTURE.md's two Mermaid diagrams against the delivered module layout, every sibling .md against its module's actual symbols, README links, and the mermaid rendering itself. Use the repo-docs-sync skill.

Original plan Further Consideration 2 suggested a CI check for markdown link integrity and mermaid syntax; decide here whether to file it.
acceptance_criteria: Both ARCHITECTURE.md diagrams match the delivered architecture; every production module has a current sibling .md naming real symbols; no broken cross-links; mermaid renders; the CI link and mermaid check is either filed as a follow-up issue or explicitly declined.

title: Add negative tests for unsupported methods, invalid params, and path constraints
description:
Cover the failure surface: unknown methods, malformed params, wrong types, missing required fields, relative paths, and paths outside the session's declared directories (Phase 2.5).

Each must produce the right error code, not merely fail. The current test suite asserts on specific JSON-RPC codes, and Phase 1.6 changes that mapping -- these tests are what verify the new mapping is coherent rather than accidental.
acceptance_criteria: Negative coverage for unknown methods, malformed and wrong-typed params, missing required fields, and both path-constraint violations; every case asserts the specific error code; the error codes match the mapping documented in the acp-protocol skill.

title: Add golden JSON-RPC transcript tests for initialize, lifecycle, streaming, and cancellation
description:
Record and assert full message transcripts for the four flows the plan's verification calls out, so ordering and payload-shape regressions surface as diffs rather than as mysterious client-side breakage.

Streaming and cancellation are where ordering actually matters: session/update notifications must not appear after the prompt response, and a cancelled turn has a specific message sequence. A transcript test catches that; a unit test typically does not.

Run transcripts over both transports if the framing differs between them.
acceptance_criteria: Golden transcripts for initialize, full session lifecycle, streaming updates, and cancellation; ordering assertions included, not just payload contents; transcripts regenerable by a documented command so intentional changes are cheap to accept; a reordering of notifications fails the suite.

title: Emit deprecation warnings from the legacy action surface
description:
Decision D4's first step. The {"action": ...} surface -- list_tools, call_tool, list_prompts, get_prompt, list_resources, read_resource, ping, returning {ok: bool} envelopes -- keeps working, but every use now warns.

Warn on a channel a WebSocket client can actually see, not just the server log: a field in the response envelope is more useful to a consumer than a log line they never read. Decide and document the removal timeline so the warning can state it.
acceptance_criteria: Every legacy action logs a deprecation warning server-side and signals deprecation in the response envelope; the warning names the JSON-RPC replacement method and the removal milestone; existing action behavior is otherwise byte-identical; README marks the action surface deprecated with a migration table.

title: Map MCP results onto ACP tool-call and content updates
description:
The translation layer between the two protocols, and the thing that makes the tool-router executor's streaming meaningful.

Map MCP tools/call results to ToolCallStart/ToolCallProgress payloads and MCP content types to ACP content blocks. The two protocols have overlapping but non-identical content models -- MCP text, image, audio, embedded resource, and resource link versus ACP's five block types -- so enumerate the mapping explicitly and decide what happens to anything unmappable.

Depends on pyacp-k5w for isError fidelity: a tool that failed must surface as a failed tool call, not a successful one carrying an error payload.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit, documented mapping table between MCP content types and ACP content blocks; MCP tool results drive correct ACP tool call status transitions; a tool returning isError true produces a failed tool call; unmappable content has a defined fallback; tests cover each content type.

title: Implement set_config_option for select and boolean variants, with config_option_update
description:
The SDK exposes this as one method taking either SetSessionConfigOptionBooleanRequest or SetSessionConfigOptionSelectRequest via @param_models, so one implementation handles both shapes -- do not write two.

Define the config options this runtime exposes, back them with the session registry's config state (Phase 2.1), and emit ConfigOptionUpdate on change. As with modes: only expose options that change behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Both request variants handled by one implementation; options are defined, advertised, and behaviorally meaningful; state persists in the session registry; ConfigOptionUpdate emitted on change; invalid config id and invalid value are rejected with the correct error; tests cover both variants.

title: Implement set_session_mode and current_mode_update propagation
description:
Implement mode switching against the session registry's mode state (Phase 2.1), and emit CurrentModeUpdate when it changes -- including when the change originates internally rather than from a client call.

Define what modes this runtime actually has. With a deterministic tool-router executor, plausible modes are things like a dry-run or read-only mode versus an execute mode; that would give the permission gating in Phase 4.1 something to key on. Do not invent modes with no behavioral difference.
acceptance_criteria: Available modes are defined with real behavioral differences and advertised at session creation; set_session_mode updates registry state and takes effect on the next turn; CurrentModeUpdate is emitted on every change including internal ones; tests cover switching mid-session and an invalid mode id.

title: Implement authenticate and logout flows
description:
initialize currently returns authMethods: [] and auth: {logout: null} -- we advertise no authentication at all. Decide whether this runtime has anything to authenticate: with no LLM and an MCP backend spawned locally, there may be no credential in the picture, in which case declining is the honest answer and this issue is about recording that decision, not writing an auth system.

If there IS something (a remote MCP backend over http/sse, for instance), implement authenticate and logout and populate authMethods for real.
acceptance_criteria: Either authenticate and logout are implemented with a populated authMethods list and tests, or the decision to decline authentication is recorded with a rationale and the capability block honestly reflects it; no aspirational literals either way.
notes: pyacp-4ns.2 (docs/acp-compliance-matrix.md) found 'logout' is unroutable at agent-client-protocol 0.12.1: AGENT_METHODS['logout'] and AgentAuthCapabilities.logout both exist, but build_agent_router registers no logout route and acp.interfaces.Agent has no logout member. Reachable only via ext_method or a hand-added route. The matrix advertises NO authMethods and leaves agentCapabilities.auth.logout null, so 'authenticate' is an explicit typed refusal and there is nothing to log out of. Recommended resolution: drop logout from this bead's scope; if it is kept, it must be justified against an auth method we actually offer.

title: Call fs/read_text_file and fs/write_text_file, gated on client capability
description:
Consume the client's filesystem methods rather than touching the filesystem directly, so the client stays in control of what is read and written.

Gate on the clientCapabilities captured at initialize (Phase 1.4) and define the fallback when the client does not offer fs -- direct filesystem access, or refusal. That choice interacts with Phase 2.5's containment rule, which is where the directory boundary is enforced.

read_text_file takes optional line and limit parameters; support them rather than always reading whole files.
acceptance_criteria: Both methods called through the client when advertised; line and limit honored on read; behavior with no fs capability is defined, documented, and tested; paths respect Phase 2.5's containment rule; a client that errors on the call does not crash the turn.
notes:
pyacp-3rw.4 settled the containment rule this bead enforces. Do not re-derive it:

    from python_acp.paths import require_contained
    resolved = require_contained(path, session.roots, "fs/read_text_file path")

- session.roots is (cwd, *additional_directories), already validated absolute and
  lexically normalised at the edge in agent.py.
- require_contained returns the RESOLVED path; use it. Re-deriving from the original
  string would open something the check never saw.
- Both sides resolve symlinks. A link inside cwd pointing at /etc/shadow is refused; a
  link inside pointing back inside is allowed; a declared root that is itself a link is
  still a live boundary. A prefix match is NOT containment. Empty roots permits nothing.
- PathConstraintError subclasses ValueError, so errors.to_request_error already answers
  -32602 with the reason in data. No special case needed.

KNOWN LIMIT this bead inherits and may need to close: containment is a CHECK, NOT A LOCK.
Resolution happens at check time, so a path that passes can become a symlink out of the
tree a microsecond later (TOCTOU). Closing it needs the fd actually opened -- openat /
O_NOFOLLOW -- which belongs with the code doing the opening, i.e. here. Documented in
src/python_acp/paths.md under "What this does not promise".

title: Call the terminal/* client method family
description:
Consume create_terminal, terminal_output, wait_for_terminal_exit, kill_terminal, and release_terminal.

Terminals are stateful and leak: a created terminal must be released on every path including turn cancellation, session close (Phase 2.3), and client disconnect. Track live terminals per session so cleanup is possible.

output_byte_limit exists on CreateTerminalRequest for a reason -- unbounded output is a real failure mode. Set it.
acceptance_criteria: All five methods callable and gated on client capability; every created terminal is released on normal completion, cancellation, session close, and disconnect; live terminals tracked per session; output_byte_limit set to a documented default; tests cover the leak paths, not just the happy path.

title: Handle all ACP content block types with capability gating
description:
Handle TextContentBlock, ImageContentBlock, AudioContentBlock, ResourceContentBlock, and EmbeddedResourceContentBlock on the way in.

The current initialize advertises promptCapabilities image, audio, and embeddedContext all false. Whatever this issue actually implements determines which of those literals flip -- and per Phase 1.4, a literal cannot be flipped without a feature test behind it. Declining a block type is a legitimate outcome as long as advertisement matches.
acceptance_criteria: Every content block type either handled or explicitly declined with the correct error; promptCapabilities literals match implemented behavior exactly; a client sending a declined type gets a clear error rather than a crash or silent drop; tests cover each type.

title: Implement the extended lifecycle: load_session, resume_session, fork_session, list_sessions, close_session
description:
The optional-but-required-for-strict-full-v1 lifecycle surface. Depends on Phase 2.1's copy-versus-share decisions.

fork_session is in the SDK's Agent protocol and was ABSENT from the original plan -- do not skip it.

Each method implemented here must flip its corresponding literal in the initialize capability block (loadSession, sessionCapabilities.delete, and so on), per Phase 1.4's rule that advertisement matches reality.
acceptance_criteria: All five methods implemented against the SDK models; each has its capability literal flipped in initialize and a test proving the feature; load and resume restore session metadata and backends correctly; fork produces an independent session per the documented semantics; list_sessions paginates via cursor; close_session releases MCP backends and terminals.
notes:
pyacp-4ns.2: close_session, fork_session, and resume_session are unstable-gated in the SDK. They are unreachable unless pyacp-tzd.1 built the connection with use_unstable_protocol=True. Verify that before implementing. fork_session was absent from the original plan and must not alias the parent session's mutable state.
pyacp-3rw.1 findings, for this bead to consume:

1. acp.contrib.session_state was evaluated and REPLACED for the registry (wrong direction:
   it consumes SessionNotifications a client receives; single-session; no cwd/dirs/config/
   timestamps/lifetime; marked experimental). BUT SessionAccumulator is a good fit for the
   HISTORY half of load_session -- feed it every SessionNotification the session sends and
   it holds the replay in a form the SDK maintains. Weigh the experimental marker before
   depending on it. See src/python_acp/sessions.md.
2. Fork/resume semantics are FIXED in sessions.py, do not rediscover them: fork = new id +
   deep copy of modes/config (they are mutated in place, a shallow copy aliases) + its own
   MCP backend instances + starts idle; resume = same object, shares everything, touch()
   only. A shared backend would make close on the fork tear down the parent's tools; a
   refcounted share is a valid optimisation only if close-independence survives.
3. SessionRegistry.list() already fixes the ordering (updated_at desc, session_id tiebreak)
   so a cursor means the same thing to every caller. Pagination itself is this bead's.
4. SessionRegistry(on_close=...) is the seam for mcp_registry teardown -- awaited with the
   session id after the entry is removed. sessions.py deliberately never imports MCP
   (module-boundaries B6a).
5. Advertising sessionCapabilities.list / .fork / .resume / .close and loadSession means
   flipping rows in capabilities.AGENT_CAPABILITY_MANIFEST *and* adding entries to
   CAPABILITY_EVIDENCE in tests/test_capabilities.py naming the tests that prove them.
   The suite fails otherwise. The three unstable ones also need use_unstable_protocol,
   which both transports already pass.
close_reason: load/list/fork/resume/close live; five capability literals flipped with evidence tests (the guard refused every flip until they existed). Session.history is an append-only list, NOT SessionAccumulator (it merges, which is the opposite of a replay). Keyset cursor pagination. fork opens its own MCP subprocesses from the parent's specs. The three unstable rows are advertised per connection via build_agent_capabilities(unstable=), a correction to the matrix noted there. 275 tests; full lifecycle verified over a spawned stdio process.

title: Enforce absolute-path and argument constraints on session inputs
description:
ACP requires absolute paths for cwd and additionalDirectories. Nothing validates them today because there is no session code at all.

Validate at the boundary and reject with the correct ACP error rather than letting a relative path reach the filesystem or an MCP subprocess cwd. Also decide and enforce whether paths outside cwd plus additionalDirectories are refused -- this is the containment boundary for Phase 4.2's fs/* calls, so it needs to be settled here, not there.
acceptance_criteria: Relative cwd or additionalDirectories are rejected with the correct ACP error code; the containment rule for paths outside the session's declared directories is documented and enforced; symlink and .. traversal cases are covered by tests; the rule is documented where Phase 4.2 can rely on it.
close_reason: paths.py + paths.md + 28 tests. Absolute-path rule enforced at the edge in agent.py for new/fork/resume/load (-32602); declared roots normalised lexically but never resolved. Containment rule settled and implemented: both sides resolve, so symlink escapes and .. traversal are refused, prefix matches are not containment, empty roots permits nothing. TOCTOU limit documented and recorded on pyacp-8bv.2 with the exact call to make. sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories flipped with an evidence test. 310 tests pass.

title: Standardize ACP/JSON-RPC error mapping on the SDK
description:
The current mapping is exception-type-driven and lossy: ValueError to -32602, MCPProtocolError to -32603, unknown method to -32601, bad JSON to -32700, bad shape to -32600. Every backend failure collapses to -32603 regardless of what the MCP server actually said.

Rebuild the mapping on the SDK's error types and the ACP-specific codes, and preserve backend fidelity -- this is the same defect pyacp-k5w tracks from the MCP side, so the two should land together or in sequence with an explicit contract between them.

The mapping is asserted by existing tests; changing it is a wire-contract change.
acceptance_criteria: Error codes are produced by one documented mapping rather than ad-hoc construction; ACP-specific error codes are used where the spec defines them; an MCP server's -32601 and -32602 remain distinguishable to the client; the mapping is documented in the rewritten acp-protocol skill; tests assert each code.
close_reason: errors.py owns every client-facing code; ws_bridge frames but no longer decides. Messages standardized on the SDK convention (concise message + data.reason); forwarded backend errors keep the server's code and message with data.source='mcp'. @as_request_error on every PythonAcpAgent request member stops acp.Connection flattening MCPProtocolError to -32603. Skill rewrite deferred to pyacp-4ns.4 (.claude/skills is sandbox write-denied).

title: Rebind the WebSocket transport onto acp.ws.server
description:
Replace the hand-rolled websockets.serve plumbing in ws_bridge.py with the SDK's acp.ws.server so both transports serve the same agent object and there is one dispatch path.

This SUPERSEDES pyacp-exl, which planned to migrate ws_bridge.py off the deprecated websockets legacy asyncio API (websockets.serve and websockets.server.WebSocketServerProtocol) onto websockets.asyncio.server. If the SDK's ws transport is already on the modern API, that migration comes free and pyacp-exl closes as superseded; if it is not, pyacp-exl's analysis still applies to whatever we bind. Resolve which before starting, and check whether the ws transport sits behind the SDK's 'http' extra.

Confirmed during pyacp-0f6: websockets 12.0 imports clean with no warnings on 3.11-3.14, so there is no urgency independent of this change.
acceptance_criteria: WebSocket clients are served by the same acp.Agent instance as stdio clients; no imports from websockets.legacy or websockets.server remain in src/; the websockets pin is on a currently supported release; pyacp-exl is closed or explicitly retained with a reason; ws_bridge.md reflects the new binding; both transports covered by tests.
notes: pyacp-4ns.3 (module boundaries) corrects this issue's premise. acp.ws.server at SDK 0.12.1 exposes only handle_asgi_websocket(server, scope, receive, send) -- an ASGI handler requiring acp.http.server.AcpServer. Rebinding literally onto it means adopting starlette/uvicorn as a runtime dependency. Decision B4 in docs/module-boundaries.md: keep the websockets library and give transport_ws.py a WebSocketMessageTransport satisfying acp._transport.Transport structurally (async send(dict)/receive()->dict|None/close()); AgentSideConnection accepts a Transport in place of a stream pair and Transport is @runtime_checkable, so we never import the private module. Also: this issue owns the git mv of ws_bridge.py -> transport_ws.py and ws_bridge.md -> transport_ws.md, the ACPWebSocketBridge class rename, and the logger rename (tests/test_mcp_stdio.py:15 and :172 depend on both). Retitle before working.
close_reason: WebSocket rebound onto acp.run_agent via WebSocketMessageTransport (decision B4 -- NOT acp.ws.server, which is ASGI-only and would pull starlette/uvicorn). ws_bridge.py git mv'd to transport_ws.py and gutted; legacy surface quarantined in legacy_ws.py, carrying the JSON-RPC MCP passthrough too so nothing working disappears before pyacp-sld.2 renames it. websockets 12.0 -> 17.0.1; no websockets.legacy/websockets.server imports remain. One PythonAcpAgent per socket (the acceptance's 'same instance' reading is not implementable -- on_connect stores one Client facade). 178 tests, 0 failures, all socket-free.

title: Rewrite the acp-protocol skill for the SDK-based contract
description:
The acp-protocol skill currently documents the hand-rolled dispatcher in detail: the two request shapes, the exception-type-to-error-code table (ValueError to -32602, MCPProtocolError to -32603), the notification handling, and a seven-step checklist for adding a method. Once dispatch comes from acp.agent.router, essentially all of that is wrong.

Rewrite it against the SDK: how to add an Agent method, where capability gating belongs, how errors map now, and how the legacy action surface behaves during its deprecation window (D4). Keep the skill's job the same -- stop agents from getting the wire contract wrong -- and keep the docs checklist, which is still correct.

Do this at the END of Phase 0 or it will be rewritten twice.
acceptance_criteria: The skill describes the SDK-based contract with no stale references to _dispatch_jsonrpc, _dispatch_legacy_action, or the exception-to-code table if it no longer applies; the add-a-method checklist matches the new module layout; the skill's frontmatter description still triggers on the same work.
notes:
pyacp-4ns.3 found the acp-protocol skill stale in two more places beyond the dispatcher rewrite. (1) It says 'Phase 0.4 freezes a JSON-RPC-only surface and Phase 1.1 removes the action API' -- that is the ORIGINAL plan; the revised plan's D4/D5 keep the action surface through the migration and remove it in Phase 7 (pyacp-sld.3). (2) Its 'Known constraints in the MCP backend' section is wrong on three of four bullets: mcp_stdio.py now has _read_loop/_handle_message/_handle_server_request so mismatched-id messages are no longer discarded, _drain_stderr exists, and request() holds _write_lock across id allocation and the write only, not across the read. Only the single-process-wide-MCP-server bullet still holds. Also rewrite target names against docs/module-boundaries.md: the error-mapping table moves to errors.md, dispatch moves to the SDK router, and ws_bridge.md becomes transport_ws.md.
SEQUENCING (decided 2026-08-22 with the user): deferred until Phase 1 lands, now blocked on pyacp-tzd.1 and pyacp-tzd.6. The bead's original 'do this at the END of Phase 0' was about not rewriting twice WITHIN Phase 0; it predates the observation that the SDK runtime it must describe (agent.py, errors.py, transport_ws.py) does not exist until Phase 1. Rewriting before then would make the skill describe modules no agent can open - the inverse of the staleness pyacp-ysp just fixed. Until tzd.1/tzd.6 land, the hand-rolled dispatcher in ws_bridge.py IS the live wire contract and the skill correctly documents it (corrected by pyacp-ysp on 2026-08-22).

title: Make the Makefile venv handling correct both in an activated venv and on a bare CI runner
description:
The Makefile assumes one environment shape and silently does the wrong thing in the other.

Local (this sandbox and any developer who has run 'source venv/bin/activate'): VIRTUAL_ENV=/Users/dave/dev/other/python-acp/venv and PATH starts with venv/bin, so the Makefile's 'PYTHON ?= python3' resolves to venv/bin/python3 -- the interpreter inside the venv make is about to manage. VENV_DIR resolves to 'venv' because that directory exists.

GitHub Actions (all four legs of the ci.yml matrix added in pyacp-0f6): a fresh checkout has neither .venv nor venv, so VENV_DIR falls through to '.venv', no venv is active, and 'python3' is whatever actions/setup-python put on PATH.

Concrete defects that follow:

1. 'make venv' never recreates an existing venv -- the recipe is guarded by 'if [ ! -d $(VENV_DIR) ]'. So 'make venv PYTHON=python3.12' on a machine that already has venv/ built from 3.14 does not build a 3.12 environment; it pip-installs into the 3.14 one and reports success. There is no supported way to reproduce a non-default matrix leg locally. Validating pyacp-0f6 required building .venv311/.venv312/.venv313 by hand, entirely outside the Makefile, precisely because of this.

2. VENV_DIR differs between the two environments ('venv' locally, '.venv' in CI) purely as a side effect of which directory happens to exist. Two developers on the same commit can be using different directories, and neither matches CI.

3. Every target depends on venv, and the venv recipe unconditionally runs 'pip install --upgrade pip' followed by 'pip install -e .[dev]'. So 'make test' always reaches the network. In a network-restricted sandbox that is a hard failure (pip cannot verify the proxy's TLS cert against Python's CA store, so make venv exits non-zero before any test runs); in CI it is wasted time on every invocation.

4. DEMO_MCP_COMMAND defaults to bare 'python3 tests/fixtures/mock_mcp_server.py' rather than $(PYTHON_BIN). 'make run' therefore launches the MCP subprocess on whatever python3 is on PATH while the bridge itself runs on $(VENV_DIR)/bin/python. Those coincide only when a venv is already activated -- exactly the local case, which is why it has never been noticed.
design:
Make the environment explicit instead of inferred.

- Pin VENV_DIR to a single default ('.venv') rather than deriving it from whichever directory exists, and keep it overridable. Decide what to do about the existing venv/ (support both for a transition, or document the rename).
- Make the venv recipe version-aware: record the interpreter used to build it (a stamp file, or read $(VENV_DIR)/bin/python --version) and rebuild when $(PYTHON) does not match, so 'make venv PYTHON=python3.12 VENV_DIR=.venv312' is the supported way to reproduce a matrix leg.
- Gate the pip install behind that stamp so lint/test/build stop hitting the network on every run; add an explicit 'make sync' or force flag for when deps genuinely changed.
- Point DEMO_MCP_COMMAND at $(PYTHON_BIN).
- If PYTHON resolves inside VENV_DIR itself (the activated-venv case), resolve it to the base interpreter or fail with a clear message rather than bootstrapping a venv from inside the venv it is replacing.

Verify by running the same make targets in both shapes: with venv activated, and in a container or fresh clone with no venv present.
acceptance_criteria: 'make venv PYTHON=<other-interpreter>' produces an environment on that interpreter even when a venv already exists, and every matrix leg from ci.yml is reproducible locally with a documented one-line command; 'make lint' and 'make test' succeed with no network access once the venv is provisioned; 'make run' launches the MCP subprocess on the venv interpreter; all four ci.yml legs stay green; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md describe the venv contract, including which directory is canonical.

title: Reconcile Python version drift: local venv 3.14 vs CI 3.11
description: Local development runs Python 3.14.6 (repo venv/bin/python, based on /opt/homebrew/bin/python3) while both GitHub Actions workflows pin python-version: 3.11 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:18, .github/workflows/publish-artifacts.yml:17). pyproject.toml declares requires-python = '>=3.11', so 3.14 is nominally in range, but nothing in CI ever exercises it. Two minor versions of drift means local green does not imply CI green (and vice versa): 3.12-3.14 removed distutils, tightened asyncio deprecations, and changed several typing behaviors this codebase touches. Decide the supported range and make CI prove it.
design: Options: (a) add a CI matrix over 3.11 + 3.14 so both the floor and the local dev version are tested; (b) pin local dev to 3.11 to match CI exactly; (c) move CI to 3.14 and raise requires-python. Recommend (a): keep requires-python '>=3.11' honest by testing the declared floor and the newest supported release, and leave publish-artifacts.yml on the floor version for the widest-compatible wheel. Verify asyncio usage in mcp_stdio.py and ws_bridge.py against 3.14 deprecations while doing this.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs the test suite on both the minimum supported Python and the version used for local development; requires-python in pyproject.toml matches the versions CI actually verifies; make lint && make test pass on every version in the matrix; CLAUDE.md's CI description is updated to reflect the matrix instead of a single 3.11 run.

title: Cover the real WebSocket opening handshake without bind()

Prefer (a) -- one transport path, no environment-dependent branching, and nothing about these tests actually needs a TCP port.

title: Close the subprocess stdin before SIGTERM in MCPStdioClient.stop
